paths.description: Homepage and global navigation, consent, search entry, weather overview; represents shared site chrome.
Helsinki location detail; represents city forecast and dense weather-data cards.
Interactive radar/map; highest-risk JavaScript, network, interaction and memory template.
Meteorologist article; represents editorial/content template and long-form reading.
Primary location-search POST flow with Turku success, nonsense-query recovery, and blank-query state.

findings.summary: High-contrast preference breaks the consent decision surface.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more screenshot collapsed the consent UI to a logo/loading panel without usable decision controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Test the CMP under prefers-contrast and forced colors; preserve readable decision controls with system colors and forced-color-adjust only where justified.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt and do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Static CSS inspection found no view-transition rules, and route changes use ordinary document navigation with abrupt swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document view transitions for same-origin forecast and article navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state-aware orientation.
findings.evidence: The 8,000-9,000 px pages retain static chrome; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or progress indicator.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or compacting-header affordance on long article and forecast templates.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent wall obscures the core weather task on every first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360x800 screenshots show a full-screen consent wall covering all weather content on first load.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-preserving consent surface where legally permissible, while keeping reject and manage choices immediately available.

findings.summary: The CMP recreates modal behavior with a div role=dialog.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection shows the CMP is a div role=dialog rather than a native dialog; dismissal is wired with custom buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog with correct initial focus, Escape/cancel behavior, inert background, and labelled description.

findings.summary: Core forecast content is surrounded by excessive repeated navigation and promotional modules.
findings.evidence: Representative pages are 8,092-9,170 px tall and repeat extensive navigation, promos, weather modules, and ad scaffolding around the core forecast.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the current forecast/article, collapse repeated secondary modules, and defer offscreen promotional sections.

findings.summary: Reusable modules rely on viewport layout rather than container-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: The shipped site CSS contains no @container or container-type signal despite cards/modules reused in main and sidebar contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for cards and weather modules reused across main/sidebar widths.

findings.summary: Several interactive targets are too short for touch.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size failed; forecast date links measure 196x23 px and many navigation links are only 13-19 px high. Focus outlines are visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls, without shrinking visible focus.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is 9.2-15.5 seconds and radar interaction readiness is poor.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 9.2-15.5 s across templates; radar TBT was 1,870 ms. CLS remained 0.003.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP resource, delay consent/ad-tech work, and reduce radar startup work until LCP is under 2.5 s.

findings.summary: Radar startup blocks the main thread with 37 long tasks.
findings.evidence: Radar trace recorded 37 long tasks, 564 ms TBT, and a 153.5 ms longest task; Lighthouse measured 1,870 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split map startup, yield between tile/style initialization phases, and move suitable processing off the main thread.

findings.summary: Large request graphs and parser-inserted dependencies delay core content.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 90-209 requests and 1.29-2.06 MB transferred; radar loads four parser-inserted stylesheets and a large map script before its dependency chain completes.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-core scripts, inline only critical CSS, and shorten the radar dependency chain; confirm each parser script async/defer requirement.

findings.summary: Pages ship 302-453 KiB of unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 302 KiB unused JS on ordinary pages and 453 KiB on radar, including ad-tech and about 154 KiB of unused glmap code.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load ads, CMP integrations, and the map bundle only when their surface is needed; tree-shake the map bundle.

findings.summary: Forecast accessible names omit visible values and radar images lack alternatives.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found visible forecast text excluded from aria-label names and two radar images without alt; probes found 13-19 unnamed controls per template.
findings.suggestedFix: Make accessible names include the visible date/value content; mark decorative map images alt="" and label meaningful controls.

findings.summary: Text contrast fails WCAG minimums across every template.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse contrast audits failed on every template, including white on #00a5f1 at 2.74:1 and white on #5eb900 at 2.49:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken blue/green backgrounds or text colors so normal text reaches 4.5:1 in both themes.

findings.summary: Heading order skips levels in forecast content.
findings.evidence: Focus probes show visible browser outlines, but Lighthouse found invalid heading order (for example H5 forecast dates after higher-level skips).
findings.suggestedFix: Use headings for document hierarchy rather than visual styling and remove empty heading elements.

findings.summary: Touch targets and radar equivalents remain incomplete despite good reflow.
findings.evidence: Reflow succeeds with no horizontal overflow, but Lighthouse target-size fails and the radar has controls/images without complete accessible equivalents.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target sizing and provide text/semantic equivalents for map state and controls.

findings.summary: Image delivery has missing dimensions, legacy formats, and oversized assets.
findings.evidence: Documents have HTML5 doctypes and UTF-8, but images audit found 15 missing dimensions, 7 oversized images, 38 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and 84 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes, modern formats, and lazy loading below the fold.

findings.summary: The radar bundle lacks a source map and the article logs DevTools issues.
findings.evidence: Radar Lighthouse reports a missing source map for the 309 KB glmap bundle; the article run reports DevTools inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish valid production source maps with controlled access and resolve the reported inspector issues.

findings.summary: Localized variants are not connected with hreflang.
findings.evidence: Canonical URLs and successful status codes are present, but none of the four pages exposes hreflang despite a language selector with many localized variants.
findings.suggestedFix: Add reciprocal hreflang links, including x-default, across Finnish and language-selector variants.

findings.summary: Core security headers and secure cookie attributes are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but the headers primitive found no CSP or HSTS and cookies audit found three cookies without Secure and all four with SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP, HSTS, nosniff, and Secure/Lax cookie attributes; verify SameSite=None is truly required.

findings.summary: Extensive tracking and ad-tech load before consent.
findings.evidence: Before consent, the page contacted 15 third-party origins including DoubleClick, GTM, Clarity, ad-tech and audience services; home transferred 1.01 MB third-party bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics, advertising, audience, and sync requests until affirmative consent; remove vendors without clear user value.

findings.summary: The document lacks clickjacking, referrer, permissions, and XSS defenses.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, nosniff, CSP, or HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP and nosniff; validate with report-only CSP first.

findings.summary: Localized versions lack hreflang and CSS is not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: Pages correctly set lang=fi, but expose no hreflang and the shipped CSS has no logical-property signals while using many physical left/right declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Connect locales with hreflang and migrate layout rules to logical properties; test an RTL locale.

findings.summary: Consent presentation favors acceptance while trackers load before choice.
findings.evidence: The first-load consent wall makes Hyväksy the blue primary action while Estä kaikki is secondary, and tracker requests occur before a choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Give accept and reject equal visual weight and prevent non-essential requests until consent.

findings.summary: Most images use legacy delivery and many are not responsive or lazy.
findings.evidence: Images audit found 84 legacy images, 38 below-fold images without lazy loading, 13 without srcset, and 7 oversized assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert photographic assets to AVIF/WebP, provide responsive sources, and lazy-load below-fold imagery.

findings.summary: Advertising and consent code creates substantial unused work.
findings.evidence: Ordinary pages load roughly 0.8 MB of script and Lighthouse estimates 302 KiB unused; much is advertising/consent code loaded before a user choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional vendors on consent and visibility, and schedule non-critical work after the core forecast is interactive.

findings.summary: Third parties dominate transferred bytes and radar requests.
findings.evidence: Home transfers 1.01 MB from third parties out of 1.29 MB total; radar transfers 1.45 MB third-party bytes and makes 168 third-party requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors, and lazy-load map frames/tiles around the active time only.

findings.summary: Radar retained heap grows 33% after repeated zoom cycles.
findings.evidence: After 10 zoom-in/zoom-out cycles and GC, radar heap self-size rose from 56.7 MB to 75.3 MB (+33%) and node count from 921,761 to 955,233.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile retained map tiles, typed arrays, listeners and caches across multiple zoom cycles; cap caches and release obsolete tile data.

taskList.title: Stop all non-essential third-party requests before consent and simplify the consent surface
Fix mobile LCP and radar main-thread startup
Deploy a complete security-header and cookie policy
Correct contrast, accessible names, headings, targets and radar alternatives
Investigate and bound radar retained-memory growth
Reduce repeated chrome and defer offscreen modules
Connect localized pages and adopt logical CSS properties
Adopt native dialog semantics and progressive navigation transitions
